text:
Sam: Heads-up, seeing sustained GPU attach failures in us-east1 for ~30m. Attach logs show NVMe IO timeouts on the scratch devices so pods never transition to Ready.
Ravi: Ugh. Any correlation with recent node firmware/driver pushes?
Sam: Yep — we rolled FW 2.3.1 to a subset of the pool ~45m ago. Errors seem concentrated on that cohort (hosts tagged fw=2.3.1).
Jun: Can you paste a representative error?
Sam: sure:
```
Attach failed: timeout waiting for block device (/dev/nvme0n1) ready, last I/O err=I/O timeout
kernel: nvme0: I/O 0 QID 10 timeout, status: 0x...
smart: media_errors increased from 0 to 18 in 10m
```
Maya: OpsBot just fired an alert too: "ephemeral-cleaner IO saturation - us-east1 - 12 hosts" :rotating_light:
OpsBot: [alert] ephemeral-cleaner throughput spike in us-east1; average iops on scratch devices 10x baseline, latency P99 > 400ms.
Ravi: That aligns with garbage-collector/cleaner overlap — when cleaner runs aggressively on some drives post-FW the GC path seems to create small-random writes that thrash device firmware, amplifying read tail latency.
Luca: Quick checks to run: `ssh node && sudo iostat -x 1 5 /dev/nvme0n1`, `sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`, and `journalctl -u ephemeral-cleaner -n 200`.
Sam: ran those on node-34 (fw=2.3.1): iostat shows util 99%, await 200ms, svctm 30ms. smart-log shows media_errors spike and a non-zero temp_warning count. Cleaner logs show deep-scan jobs started concurrently.
Jun: Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle cleaner concurrency on fw=2.3.1 cohort (janitor.max_workers=1) 2) temporarily exclude cohort from GPU attach (route policy to other nodes/regions) 3) roll back FW on the worst offenders.
Maya: Can we do (1) quickly? How to scope it?
Ravi: We have a weighted-config flag: `ephemeral.cleaner.concurrency.override[region=\"us-east1\",fw=\"2.3.1\"] = 1`. Apply via config push; takes ~90s to propagate to janitor controllers.
Luca: I'll prepare the patch and gate it under canary: apply to 5 nodes first, watch iops. Also recommend a temporary attach-routing change: add a policy to prefer us-central for new GPU allocs for 1h.
Sam: sounds good. Cost tradeoffs: diverting to us-central will increase cross-region egress and cold-starts for some customers — estimate ~+$850/hr if sustained. But risk of failed attaches is worse.
Jun: Agree. Also open a ticket to get FW vendor involved — media_errors + temp warnings smell like GC-FW interaction.
Maya: After throttling, what success metric? iops down to <3x baseline and attach success rate >95% for 10m?
Ravi: Yes. Also monitor `attach_latency_p50/p99` and `nvme.media_errors`. If media_errors stop climbing and attach rate recovers, we can slowly restore concurrency.
Sam: Action items: Luca will push concurrency override & attach-route change (WIP). Jun files vendor ticket with sample smart logs. Maya monitors metrics and pings oncall if anything regresses.
Luca: pushing patch now (`cfg push ephemeral.cleaner override`) -> rolling to controllers. tagging nodes: `fw=2.3.1`.
OpsBot: [deploy] config push detected by CI: ephemeral.cleaner.override -> rollout started.
Maya: Watching dashboards — starting to see util drop on the 5-canary nodes after ~3m. p99 latency falling from 420ms to 90ms.
Sam: Nice. Keep the route preference in place until we confirm full cohort is stable.
Ravi: We'll plan a controlled FW rollback for nodes that don't recover after vendor guidance.
Jun: Prep postmortem template now — include timeline, FW cohort list, cleaner tuning, cost impact estimate.
Maya: Thanks all — will update thread with vendor ticket number and final decision on rollback. :white_check_mark:
